This chapter repeats the Lab 2 steps from [`model-vetiver.qmd`](model-vetiver.qmd) in R. The source Quarto document can be found in [`_labs/lab02/R/model-vetiver-r.qmd`](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/blob/main/_labs/lab02/R/model-vetiver-r.qmd).

```{r}
#| collapse: true
#| eval: false
fs::dir_tree("_labs/lab02/R/")
## _labs/lab02/R/
## └── model-vetiver-r.qmd
```

## Load packages 

```{r}
#| message: false 
#| warning: false
#| eval: true
library(palmerpenguins)
library(plumber)
library(dplyr)
library(duckdb)
library(fastDummies)
library(vetiver)
library(pins)
```


## Get Data

We load the `palmerpenguins` data and create a connection with `dbConnect()`. Then we register the R data frame with `duckdb` and create the `penguins` table:

```{r}
#| eval: false
penguins_data <- palmerpenguins::penguins

con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "my-db.duckdb")

duckdb_register(con, "penguins_data", penguins_data)

dbExecute(con, "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE penguins AS SELECT * FROM penguins_data")
```

We then read the `penguins` table back with `dbGetQuery()`, drop missing rows with `na.omit()`, and disconnect from the database:

```{r}
#| eval: false
df <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM penguins") |>
  na.omit()

dbDisconnect(con)
```

We can confirm the data loaded by viewing the top rows of `df`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
head(df, 3)
```

::: {style="font-style: italic;"}

```{verbatim}
  species    island bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm body_mass_g
1  Adelie Torgersen           39.1          18.7               181        3750
2  Adelie Torgersen           39.5          17.4               186        3800
3  Adelie Torgersen           40.3          18.0               195        3250
     sex year
1   male 2007
2 female 2007
3 female 2007
```

:::

## Define Model and Fit

Next, we create dummy variables (one-hot encoding) for `species` and `sex` and fit a linear regression model that predicts `body_mass_g`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
X <- df |>
  select(bill_length_mm, species, sex) |>
  dummy_cols(
    select_columns = c("species", "sex"), 
    remove_first_dummy = TRUE) |>
  select(-species, -sex)

y <- df$body_mass_g

model <- lm(y ~ ., data = X)
```

## Extract model fit statistics

We pull the R-squared, intercept, coefficients, and column names from the fitted model:

```{r}
#| eval: false
r_squared <- summary(model)$r.squared
intercept <- coef(model)[1]
coefficients <- coef(model)[-1]
column_names <- names(X)
```

Then we print each statistic to the console with `cat()`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
cat("R^2:", r_squared, "\n")
cat("Intercept:", intercept, "\n")
cat("Columns:", paste(column_names, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Coefficients:", paste(coefficients, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

The output should match the Python model in [`model-vetiver.qmd`](model-vetiver.qmd):

::: {style="font-style: italic;"}

```{verbatim}
R^2: 0.8555369
Intercept: 2169.27
Columns: bill_length_mm, species_Chinstrap, species_Gentoo, sex_male
Coefficients: 32.5368867712031, -298.765534465279, 1094.86739144898, 547.36692407721
```

:::

## Turn into Vetiver Model

`vetiver_model()` wraps the fitted `lm()` object into a deployable `vetiver` model named `penguin_model`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| message: false 
#| warning: false
v <- vetiver_model(model, model_name = "penguin_model")
```

## Save to Board

`board_folder()` creates a `pins` board in a local `models/` folder, and `vetiver_pin_write()` writes `v` to it:

```{r}
#| eval: false
model_board <- board_folder("./models")
vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v)
```

Below we can see the model information stored in the `models/` folder:

```{r}
#| collapse: true
fs::dir_tree("_labs/lab02/R/models/")
```

## Turn model into API

Unlike Python, R needs a `plumber` router (the object that holds an API's endpoints) from `plumber::pr()`. We pipe the router into `vetiver_api()` along with the deployable `vetiver_model()` object:

```{r}
#| eval: false
app <- pr() |>
  vetiver_api(v)
```

## Recap

1. Getting the data into `duckdb` from R takes one extra step: `duckdb_register()` exposes the `penguins_data` data frame to the connection before `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` builds the table. `na.omit()` then drops the missing rows (Python used `dropna()`).

2. `fastDummies::dummy_cols()` with `remove_first_dummy = TRUE` replaces `get_dummies(drop_first = True)`, and `lm()` replaces `LinearRegression()`. The model information comes from `summary(model)$r.squared` and `coef()` instead of the `scikit-learn` attributes.

3. `vetiver_model()`, `board_folder()`, and `vetiver_pin_write()` mirror the Python functions. The API step differs: R needs a `plumber` router from `plumber::pr()` piped into `vetiver_api()`, while Python's `VetiverAPI()` builds the API directly from the model.

Next, [Lab 3: Databases and APIs](lab03.qmd) builds Shiny apps in Python and R that send requests to these APIs.
